rules: The National Polygon Service is updated on the second working day of each month and contains data for the previous month.
The complete file includes all changes that happened during the month.
The change-only file contains only data changed since the previous monthly release.
The validation file is provided to check that the dataset downloaded correctly.
The Title Number and UPRN Look Up dataset does not have a change-only file.
The National Polygon Service download includes an Esri shapefile and CSV files.
API-key access requires an agreed licence, payment and a signed-in account.
The UPRN lookup dataset is closely linked to the National Polygon and Title Descriptor datasets.
The title number is a unique identifier that can link to other HM Land Registry data.
Licensed UPRN customers receive the full dataset and validation files.
The UPRN full-file name follows LR_UPRN_FULL_<three-character-month>.csv.
The UPRN validation-file name follows LR_UPRN_VALI_<three-character-month>.csv.
Entity search is exposed as a GET request to /entity.{extension}.
A single entity is retrieved through /entity/{entity}.{extension}.
The single-entity endpoint requires an integer entity identifier.
The single-entity endpoint supports json, html and geojson extensions.
Dataset listing is exposed as GET /dataset.{extension}.
The dataset-list endpoint supports json and html extensions.
A specific dataset is retrieved through /dataset/{dataset}.{extension}.
The specific-dataset endpoint supports json and html extensions.
A longitude point-intersection filter requires latitude to be supplied.
A latitude point-intersection filter requires longitude to be supplied.
Fields explicitly selected by field take precedence over exclude_field entries.
The pagination offset parameter is an optional integer.
The time-stamped DTM archive contains Environment Agency site-specific surveys across England since 1998.
Time-stamped DTM data is available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m resolutions depending on project requirements.
The DTM is produced from the last-return LIDAR signal.
Surface objects are removed using bespoke algorithms and manual editing to create a terrain-only model.
Time-stamped DTM data is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km ZIP files.
Elevation values are in metres and referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The raster data is aligned to the OS National Grid.
The metadata records vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
The transformation applied is specific to the survey time period.
The metadata catalogue identifies survey dates, resolution, transformation and geoidal model by location.
The dataset coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The official metadata identifier is dbadf364-0192-4bcf-a223-f3d403f08682.
The time-stamped point-cloud archive contains highly accurate x, y and z points with component attributes.
Environment Agency time-stamped DSM and DTM raster products are derived from point-cloud data.
Point-cloud surveys are available going back to 2006.
Historic archiving means not every DSM or DTM surface necessarily has a matching point cloud.
Processing classifies laser returns into ground and surface-object classes.
Manual editing of the derived DTM means classified ground points do not necessarily match the final DTM.
Point clouds are supplied as 5km download ZIP files for each survey year.
Downloaded archives contain LAZ files aligned to the Ordnance Survey grid.
Coverage metadata records survey flight dates and information such as average point density.
ASCII-grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
A 10km OS Terrain 50 ASCII tile contains 200 columns.
A 10km OS Terrain 50 ASCII tile contains 200 rows.
The ASCII-grid cell size is 50 metres.
Each grid tile includes an Esri ASCII .asc data file.
Each grid tile includes a .prj file containing the spatial reference system.
Each grid tile includes an .asc.aux.xml styling-parameter file.
Each grid tile includes a metadata XML file with information such as flying date.
A shapefile .shp component stores feature geometry.
A shapefile .shx component stores the feature-geometry index.
A shapefile .dbf component stores feature attributes.
A shapefile .prj component stores projection information.
The auxiliary XML supplies min, max, mean and standard-deviation height statistics to support consistent styling across adjacent tiles.
